decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “bookmark library with CRUD operations”; Round 1 client: “saving links … That all reads right.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: saving bookmarks is aligned with saving by URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker only says “CRUD operations”; Round 1 client generally approves “editing.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: the record does not enumerate whether every required editable field, particularly note, is covered.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “CRUD operations”; Round 1 client: “deleting … reads right.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: deletion is included without a conflicting behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “tags”; Round 1 client approves “finding them by … tags.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: bookmark tagging is included and no mismatch is presented.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “filtering”; Round 1 client approves “finding them by … tags.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: tag-based filtering is aligned with the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “search”; Round 1 client says “finding them by search … reads right.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: neither side identifies which bookmark fields are searched, so conformity with the required title/description/note/URL scope cannot be established.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “sorting”; Round 1 client says “sorting … reads right.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: sortable bookmark listing conforms at the presented level.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker specifies “duplicate warnings”; Round 1 client says “the duplicate warning … reads right.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: warning about a duplicate is presented instead of guiding the user into editing the existing bookmark. The approval does not mention that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker scopes the app without automatic metadata; Round 1 client: “automatic page info is listed as excluded — I’d like it back in,” requesting automatic title and description retrieval.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the client restores a missing reference capability, although the requested correction mentions only title and description.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker omits read state; Round 1 client: “I’d want to mark some as ‘to read’.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: the client requests the missing ability to mark bookmarks for later reading.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker omits a separate unread view; Round 1 client asks to “see just those in one place.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: the client requests the missing filtered Read Later view.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker omits completion of unread items; Round 1 client asks to “mark them done.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: the client requests the missing transition from unread to read.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “import/export … deferred”; Round 1 client: “Everything else in the excluded list I’m fine setting aside for now.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: the client explicitly acknowledges the remaining exclusions and accepts deferring import.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “import/export … deferred”; Round 1 client: “Everything else in the excluded list I’m fine setting aside for now.”
decisions.note: Specification gate: the client explicitly acknowledges the remaining exclusions and accepts deferring export.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker revises metadata collection to “Automatic title and description retrieval”; Round 2 client calls title and description retrieval “exactly what I was after.”
decisions.note: Revised-specification gate: the decision still omits automatic favicon and preview-image collection. The client does not identify that remaining difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker promises “editable results” for fetched title and description; Round 2 client confirms they remain “editable.”
decisions.note: Revised-specification gate: editable collected metadata aligns with the reference, together with the previously presented editing capability.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker adds persistent “Untracked, To Read, and Read states”; Round 2 client approves marking items “To Read.”
decisions.note: Revised-specification gate: the tri-state representation is functionally equivalent to marking a bookmark unread.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker adds “a dedicated Read Later view”; Round 2 client approves “a proper ‘read later’ list.”
decisions.note: Revised-specification gate: the separate unread-bookmark view conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says items can be completed “without removing them from the library”; Round 2 client approves marking items Read “without them vanishing from my library.”
decisions.note: Revised-specification gate: marking an item read removes it from Read Later while preserving the bookmark.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents the implemented “automatic metadata retrieval with secure fallback,” carrying forward the title/description-only specification; Round 5 client discusses only “automatic title/description fetch” and approves it.
decisions.note: Implementation review: favicon and preview-image collection remain outside the presented metadata behavior, and the client does not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker lists “Read Later”; Round 5 client confirms it shows items marked “to read.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: marking bookmarks for later reading conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker lists “Read Later”; Round 5 client reports “The Read Later view shows only what I’ve marked ‘to read.’”
decisions.note: Implementation review: the dedicated unread view conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker lists “Read Later”; Round 5 client reports that marking an item Read makes it “drop out of that view but stay in my full library.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: the read transition conforms exactly.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker claims “search”; Round 5 client tests a title match and a no-result term, but neither presentation nor response establishes searching description, note, and URL.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the indexed-field scope remains indeterminate.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents implemented search; Round 5 client reports that it “ignores capitalization” and that searching “EXAMPLE” found “Example Site.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: the observed search behavior is case-insensitive.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker lists “multi-tag filtering”; Round 5 client confirms “Filtering by tag … behave[s].”
decisions.note: Implementation review: multi-tag filtering includes the reference-conforming ability to filter by a specific tag.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker lists “sorting”; Round 5 client confirms “sorting by title” works.
decisions.note: Implementation review: sorting by a supported key conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker lists “editing”; the Round 5 client gives no field-by-field editing result.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the record does not establish whether URL, title, description, tags, and note are all editable.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker lists implemented “duplicate handling,” following the warning-based specification; Round 5 client reports that resaving “warns me it’s already there instead of silently duplicating.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: duplicate creation is prevented, but no guidance into editing the existing bookmark is presented or requested.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker lists “confirmed deletion”; Round 5 client verifies “Deleting removes it for good.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: permanent deletion conforms; confirmation is an additional non-conflicting safeguard.
